title: Distributed Data Parallel and FSDP from Scratch

questions.question: Which collectives maintain the core invariant of MinimalDDP?
options: An all_gather of activations followed by reduce_scatter of labels.
Only broadcast at the end of training, because gradients are local.
A barrier before every layer and a point-to-point send after every batch.
broadcast at construction and averaged all_reduce of gradients after backward.
questions.explanation: MinimalDDP broadcasts parameters from rank 0 when constructed. The trainer then calls sync_grads, which sums each gradient across ranks and divides by world_size before stepping.

questions.question: Why can the distributed demo use the Gloo backend on a CPU-only machine?
options: Gloo implements process-group collectives over CPU tensors; the demo starts real worker processes without requiring CUDA.
Gloo is a tokenizer that replaces torch.distributed on CPU.
The demo skips all collectives when CUDA is unavailable and compares printed seeds instead.
Gloo runs only inside a single process, so rank communication is not involved.
questions.explanation: The demo initializes torch.distributed with Gloo and uses CPU tensors. It is still a multi-process collective run; NCCL is the GPU-oriented alternative.

questions.question: What does manual_all_reduce_matches_single_process compare?
options: The wall time of Gloo and NCCL on the same host.
Per-rank averaged gradients after an all-reduce against the gradient from the concatenated full batch.
The final loss after two unrelated random initializations.
The number of parameters before and after broadcasting.
questions.explanation: Each rank computes a gradient on its data slice, the helper averages those gradients, and it compares them with a single-process full-batch gradient within tolerance.

questions.question: Why does fsdp_round_trip_sketch pad a flattened parameter before all_gather?
options: Padding lets the sketch use unequal shard lengths and therefore saves communication.
Padding changes the model vocabulary so every rank owns different tokens.
It makes every rank's output buffer the same length, after which the gathered padding is removed.
It avoids broadcasting the initial parameters by regenerating them from a seed.
questions.explanation: The sketch computes equal per lengths, right-pads when the number of elements is not divisible by world_size, gathers equal-sized slices, and trims the reconstructed tensor back to its original shape.

questions.question: What does a near-zero param_sum_spread in the demo check?
options: That the model's loss is below the validation threshold.
That the network has reached its maximum bandwidth.
That FSDP never materialized a full parameter during its round trip.
That all ranks report nearly identical parameter sums after the synchronized updates.
questions.explanation: The metric is a parity check, not a quality or throughput score. A small spread supports the broadcast-and-gradient-reduction invariant across ranks.

questions.question: What does the demo's fsdp_round_trip_sketch verify for each parameter?
options: That every rank can rebuild the original flattened parameter from padded equal-sized shards.
That a parameter is permanently stored on one rank and never gathered.
That parameter names are identical to a published GPT-2 checkpoint.
That the optimizer can update sharded tensors without a gradient reduction.
questions.explanation: The sketch clones a full parameter, pads and slices it, calls all_gather, drops padding, and checks torch.allclose against the original tensor.
